categories.label: Editions
categories.description: Fedora Editions are the official OS editions of Fedora Linux.

links.label: Workstation
links.description: The flagship Fedora edition featuring the latest Gnome desktop. The Linux desktop you've been waiting for.

links.label: Server
links.description: Run applications on bare metal or the cloud with a Linux server OS packed with the latest open source technology.

links.label: IoT
links.description: A foundation for Internet of Things and Device Edge ecosystem.

links.label: Core Os
links.description: An automatically-updating, minimal operating system for running containerized workloads securely and at scale.

links.label: Cloud
links.description: An automatically-updating, minimal operating system for running containerized workloads securely and at scale.

categories.label: Emerging Editions
categories.description: These editions are supported but not yet a part of the official Fedora editions.

links.label: Silverblue
links.description: Fedora Silverblue is an immutable desktop operating system aimed at good support for container-focused workflows.

categories.label: Desktop Spins
categories.description: The Desktop spins feature specific Linux Desktop Environments. Our official Workstation Edition uses the Gnome Desktop, but you can install Fedora preconfigured with any of the listed Desktop Environments.

categories.label: Fedora Labs
categories.description: The Labs are Fedora Linux set up with software bundles based on particular topics.

community.label: Community
community.description: Our community links connect you with our communication platforms, articles, blog posts, and events.

categories.label: Communications
categories.description: Our community is big and there are many ways that we connect with one another.

categories.label: Publications
categories.description: The Fedora Project publishes content regularly in the Community Blog and Fedora Magazine. Stay up to date with the latest in the Fedora Community.

categories.label: Events
categories.description: From our release parties to our annual conference and more, Fedorans regularly come together to celebrate our community and the hard work that we put into it.

categories.label: Extended Community
categories.description: Beyond the official channels for Fedorans to communicate, community members are involved on other popular platforms as well!

contributors.label: Contributors
contributors.description: These pages connect you to all the different spaces that Fedorans work on projects. From new to long-term contributors, the following links will get you to where you want to go.

categories.description: Ask Fedora is a message board for getting help from the community.  you need help installing, using, or customizing Fedora Linux, or have any other questions about the operating system or the Fedora Project, you’ve come to the right place!

categories.description: Over the years, Fedorans have created many sources of information for using our operating system. While these are not the official support sources, they are used and maintained by members of our community.
